summary: Recursive merge sort over a singly linked list whose nodes carry a next pointer at node+4 and a payload pointer at node+0; the sort key is the float at payload+4. Returns the new list head. A null input, or a list with fewer than 2 nodes, is returned unchanged. The list is split at its midpoint, both halves are sorted recursively, then merged back in ascending key order.

operations.description: Return the input pointer unchanged when it is null.
Count the list nodes by walking the next pointer at node+4 (this+0x4).
Return the list unchanged when the count is below 2 nodes.
Advance to the midpoint node by following next pointers for half the list length.
Split the list: save the second-half head read from the midpoint next pointer and clear that next pointer to terminate the first half.
Recursively sort the first half of the list.
Recursively sort the second half of the list.
During merge, return the non-null half when the other half is null.
Merge the two sorted halves in ascending order, repeatedly selecting the head with the smaller float key; the payload pointer is read from node+0 and the key is read at payload+4.
Link each selected node behind the running merge tail through the next pointer at node+4.
Return the head of the merged (or otherwise resulting) list.
